Page 2 | Town Clerk: (585) 340-8629 | clerk@penfield.org | www.penfield.org PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T-164 DATE: November 4, 2026 BY Councilperson Getz Law and Finance Committee NAME Budget Transfers for the General Fund WHEREAS, the Town Board desires to have an up-to-date budget in relation to current income and expenditures, NOW, BE IT RESOLVED, that the following 2026 budget transfers be approved: Moved: ___ Seconded: ___ Vote: Berry Dean Getz Lang Teglash ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ PENFIELD TOWN BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 26T- 165 DATE: November 4, 2026 BY: Councilperson Getz Law & Finance Committee NAME: Express the Town Board’s intention for completion of real property revaluations every four years, beginning in 2028 WHEREAS, the Town of Penfield recognizes the importance of maintaining accurate and equitable assessments of real property to promote fairness in the distribution of the property tax burden; and WHEREAS, regular revaluations help ensure that assessments reflect changes in market values and that property owners are treated equitably in accordance with applicable New York State law; and WHEREAS, establishing a consistent revaluation schedule provides greater predictability for property owners and supports responsible municipal planning and budgeting; and WHEREAS, the Town Board believes that completing a townwide real property revaluation every four years is a reasonable and appropriate goal for maintaining equitable assessments; and WHEREAS, the Town Board intends to establish 2028 as the starting year for this fouryear revaluation cycle, with subsequent revaluations intended for 2032, 2036, and every four years thereafter; and WHEREAS, New York State offers Aid for Cyclical Reassessments to qualifying municipalities that commit to an approved recurring reassessment program; and WHEREAS, the Town Assessor agrees with the Town Board on these matters, NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Town Board of the Town of Penfield hereby expresses its intention that townwide real property revaluations be completed every four years, beginning in 2028 and continuing on a four-year cycle thereafter; BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town Board intends to work with the Town Assessor and other appropriate officials to plan and implement this schedule, subject to applicable law, available resources, and the adoption of necessary annual budgets and appropriations; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Town Board recognizes the importance of communicating the revaluation schedule to residents and providing appropriate public information regarding the assessment process and its implications for individual property owners.
